overall_structure.value: Austenite (FCC) matrix containing two types of ferrite — granular α ferrite grains and banded δ ferrite elongated along RD — in a partially recrystallized condition; shear bands retained from cold rolling. Annealing at 950 °C for 1 min produces the coarsest δ and α grains together with a large ferrite amount, and cracks are easily initiated at the α/γ interfaces.

unmapped_findings: Specific yield strength (SYS) of DP950-1 = 159.6 ± 0.8 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ (Table 1, b0019).
Specific ultimate tensile strength (SUTS) of DP950-1 = 226.4 ± 1.6 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ (Table 1, b0019).
DP950–1 has the highest ultimate tensile strength (UTS) but the lowest total elongation (TE) among the annealed specimens (b0025).

The large ferrite content of DP950–1 (and DP950–5) causes incompatible straining at the many ferrite/unRexed austenite interfaces, leading to easy crack initiation and propagation and hence poor ductility (b0025).
The engineering stress-strain curve of DP950-1 (black curve) rises steeply and terminates below about 7 % strain (Fig. 3a, figure_003).

In the SUTS-vs-TE comparison plot, DP950-1 lies among the 'Our steel' red-star data points (labelled DP950-1) clustered at the top-right, though it is not beyond the 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% contour (Fig. 3b, figure_003).
The DP950-1 specimen retains shear bands from cold rolling, as labelled in its EBSD phase map (Fig. 2b1, figure_002).
